::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 4th [1882?][^2]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne	Winchester  
**Manuscript:** UCLA: collection 100: box 95[^1]
:::

My dear [Miss Gatty](people/person_469.qmd),

The Signora [Linda Villari](people/person_1444.qmd) wife to [Professor Villari](people/person_2345.qmd) at Florence sent me this pretty little sketch of a real favourite bird. It is too youthful for the [Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd), but I think you will like to open a connection with her, as she writes prettily and freshly. I enclose a card she sent with her address. She wrote a very pretty story once for the Packet called [the Angel of Viareggio](other_books/otherbook_917.qmd).

I hope you can give a tolerable account of [Mrs Ewing](people/person_494.qmd). We were greatly charmed with Laetus Sorte Meâ<sup>3</sup>

Yours sincerely 
C M Yonge

On second thought I will keep the card as if rejected you had better return Dinderino to me

---

[^1]: Endorsed in another hand ' Signora Linda Villari/ 93r Via Tinti/ Florence/ “Dinderino”'
[^2]: ‘The Angel of Viareggio’ appeared in *MP* (January-June 1880) and ‘Laetus Sorte Mea’ in *Aunt Judy’s Magazine* in 1882.  It was published as *The Story of a Short Life* (1882).  The letter must antedate the death of Juliana Ewing in May 1885.
